answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a hollow, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so someone cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 452 aliases as a result costs 211 bonds held for 14 days each, plus the zephyr attestations those aliases can never earn. A single knoll checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
